sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Retinoblastoma (RB) is a malignant tumor of the neurosensory retina arising from primitive multipotential photoreceptor precursors (retinoblasts). It is driven by the biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 13q14. It is the most common primary intraocular malignancy of childhood, with 95% of cases diagnosed before age 5.

sections.title: Molecular Pathogenesis: Knudson's Two-Hit Hypothesis
content: 1. Germline/First Hit: Inherited mutation in one allele of RB1 gene (all cells).
2. Somatic/Second Hit: Spontaneous mutation in the remaining allele within a retinal cell.
3. Loss of Heterozygosity (LOH): Complete loss of pRB protein function.
4. Unregulated Cell Cycle: E2F transcription factors remain active, driving S-phase entry.
5. Malignant Transformation: Formation of retinoblastoma tumor clones.

sections.title: Low Penetrance Retinoblastoma
content: Phenotype where mutation carriers do not develop tumors or develop benign retinomas.
Often associated with specific RB1 mutations (e.g., promoter mutations or missense).
Risk to offspring remains high even if parent is clinically normal.
Requires careful molecular testing of 'unaffected' family members.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: 1. EUA (Examination Under Anesthesia): Scleral depression and 360° fundus drawing.
2. B-Scan Ultrasonography: Detect high-reflectivity calcium peaks.
3. Wide-field Digital Imaging (RetCam): For documentation and staging.
4. MRI Orbits & Brain: Rule out trilateral RB (pineoblastoma) and optic nerve invasion.
5. Genetic Testing: Mandatory for both somatic (tumor) and germline (blood) DNA.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Indicators for Enucleation
content: Neovascular Glaucoma (NVG)
Tumor invasion of the Anterior Chamber
Phthisis Bulbi or Pre-phthisical state
Opaque media preventing monitoring
Suspected Optic Nerve involvement on MRI

sections.title: Modern Management Paradigms
content: Intravenous Chemotherapy (IVC): Carboplatin, Vincristine, Etoposide (VEC).
Intra-arterial Chemotherapy (IAC): Melphalan/Topotecan via ophthalmic artery.
Intravitreal Chemotherapy: For recalcitrant vitreous seeds.
Local Therapy: Cryotherapy (anterior) or Laser Photocoagulation/TTP (posterior).
Plaque Brachytherapy: For localized salvage.

sections.title: Trilateral Retinoblastoma
sections.content: A rare association of bilateral RB (germline) with a midline intracranial neuroectodermal tumor (usually in the pineal gland). Requires routine neuroimaging (MRI) every 6 months until age 5 in germline-positive patients.

sections.title: Second Malignant Neoplasms
content: Lifetime risk for germline patients: ~30-50%.
Most common: Osteosarcoma, Soft tissue sarcoma, Melanoma.
Risk is significantly increased by external beam radiation therapy (EBRT).
Strict UV protection and lifelong surveillance are mandatory.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls for Boards
content: RB is the most common cause of leukocoria in children.
Avoid FNA/Biopsy: High risk of extraocular tumor seeding.
Endophytic Growth: Tumor grows into the vitreous (white seeds).
Exophytic Growth: Tumor grows toward subretinal space (serous detachment).
Regression Patterns: Type 1 (Cottage cheese/calcified), Type 2 (Fish-flesh/non-calcified), Type 3 (Mixed), Type 4 (Atrophic/Chorioretinal scar).
